name: es30-pixel-buffer-objects
title: Pixel buffer objects: texture uploads and read-backs through buffer objects
summary: PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER as the source of glTexImage2D/3D and glTexSubImage2D (the pointer is a byte offset; UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH/SKIP_PIXELS/SKIP_ROWS/ALIGNMENT/IMAGE_HEIGHT/SKIP_IMAGES select sub-rectangles and sub-volumes of a larger image in the buffer) and PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER as the destination of glReadPixels read back with glMapBufferRange and compared byte for byte, the asynchronous fence + two-buffer pattern, buffer bindings, pixel-store queries and the defined INVALID_OPERATION / INVALID_VALUE errors.
spec: ES 3.0 §3.7.1 Pixel Storage Modes and Pixel Buffer Objects (Table 3.1; INVALID_VALUE for out-of-range modes)
ES 3.0 §3.7.2.1 Unpacking (equations 3.12 and 3.13; offset in the unpack buffer; INVALID_OPERATION for ranges beyond the buffer and for offsets not divisible by the type size)
ES 3.0 §3.8.3 Texture Image Specification (TexImage3D UNPACK_IMAGE_HEIGHT / SKIP_IMAGES; TexImage2D ignores SKIP_IMAGES; data is an offset when a buffer is bound), §3.8.5 (TexSubImage)
ES 3.0 §4.3.2 Reading Pixels, §4.3.2.4 Placement in Pixel Pack Buffer or Client Memory (Table 4.4; INVALID_OPERATION for ranges beyond the buffer and unaligned offsets)

ES 3.0 §2.10 Buffer Objects (2.10.1 deletion resets bindings and zero-bound errors, 2.10.2 BufferSubData on a mapped range, 2.10.3 MapBufferRange / UnmapBuffer, 2.10.3.2 effects of mapping), Tables 2.6 and 6.16 (PIXEL_*_BUFFER_BINDING)
ES 3.0 §5.2 Sync Objects and Fences (FenceSync, ClientWaitSync)
ES 3.0 §2.1.6.2 Conversion from Floating-Point to Normalized Fixed-Point

api.glGenBuffers: unpack buffers (images, RGB, RGBA4), the round-trip buffer and per-test pack buffers
api.glBindBuffer: PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER / PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER bindings read back with glGetIntegerv; independent targets; one buffer on both targets; the pointer arguments become byte offsets only while a buffer is bound
api.glBufferData: chart / RGB / RGBA4 uploads into unpack buffers (observed through the textures), size-only pack buffers filled with a sentinel, exact boundary sizes for the INVALID_OPERATION tests; zero-bound -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glBufferSubData: INVALID_OPERATION when the range is mapped
api.glDeleteBuffers: deleting a buffer bound to both pixel targets resets both bindings to 0
api.glMapBufferRange: READ mapping of pack buffers (whole and a 16..80 sub-range): contents compared byte for byte with the CPU placement; a second map -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glUnmapBuffer: returns TRUE for an intact mapping; unmapping an unmapped buffer -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glGetBufferParameteriv: BUFFER_SIZE / BUFFER_USAGE through either pixel target, BUFFER_MAPPED false -> true, MAP_OFFSET 16 / MAP_LENGTH 64; buffer 0 bound -> INVALID_OPERATION
api.glGetBufferPointerv: MAP_POINTER equals the pointer glMapBufferRange returned and is NULL after unmapping
api.glPixelStorei: UNPACK_ROW_LENGTH / SKIP_PIXELS / SKIP_ROWS / ALIGNMENT / IMAGE_HEIGHT / SKIP_IMAGES and PACK_ROW_LENGTH / SKIP_PIXELS / SKIP_ROWS / ALIGNMENT change the buffer layouts exactly as eq. 3.12-3.13 predict; negative values and alignments 3 and 16 -> INVALID_VALUE
api.glGetIntegerv: initial and set values of all UNPACK_* and PACK_* modes (meta-gl gap G1), PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER_BINDING, PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER_BINDING, ARRAY_BUFFER_BINDING unaffected
api.glGenTextures: seven textures filled from buffers, scratch and volume textures
api.glTexImage2D: from a PIXEL_UNPACK_BUFFER with a byte offset (0, 5, 6, 4160), ROW_LENGTH / SKIP / ALIGNMENT; RGBA8, RGB8 and RGBA4 (UNSIGNED_SHORT_4_4_4_4); textures read back exactly through a framebuffer or compared as drawn; range and alignment errors
api.glTexSubImage2D: patch from a buffer with ROW_LENGTH / SKIP into an existing texture (rest unchanged); range and offset-alignment errors leave the texture unchanged
api.glTexImage3D: sub-volume of a 6x5x3 volume in a buffer with ROW_LENGTH, IMAGE_HEIGHT, SKIP_PIXELS / ROWS / IMAGES: every texel of both layers compared
api.glTexParameteri: NEAREST / CLAMP_TO_EDGE (typed overloads) so one-level textures are complete (observed through the drawn cells)
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: attaches an uploaded texture to read its texels back exactly
api.glFramebufferTextureLayer: attaches the layers of the uploaded 3D texture
api.glGenFramebuffers: framebuffers for reading textures back, the RGBA8UI test and the asynchronous frames
api.glBindFramebuffer: read / draw targets of the checks
api.glClearBufferuiv: RGBA8UI framebuffer cleared to (7, 150, 255, 33); the values are read back exactly with RGBA_INTEGER / UNSIGNED_INT into a pack buffer
api.glReadPixels: into a PIXEL_PACK_BUFFER at byte offsets with PACK_ROW_LENGTH / SKIP / ALIGNMENT (RGBA/UNSIGNED_BYTE and RGBA_INTEGER/UNSIGNED_INT): mapped bytes compared with the CPU model; round trip into the unpack buffer of a texture; range / alignment errors
api.glFenceSync: fence after each queued read-back of the asynchronous pattern
api.glClientWaitSync: returns ALREADY_SIGNALED or CONDITION_SATISFIED before the previous frame's buffer is mapped
api.glClearColor: frame colors of the asynchronous pattern, read back +-1
api.glClear: COLOR_BUFFER_BIT of each frame; the read-back colors differ per frame
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLE_STRIP quad per cell; every pixel compared
api.glViewport: per-cell viewports of texture size times scale; pixel positions verified

visual_review.notes: Viewed at 800x800 (llvmpipe, 3x3 cells of 266 px: chart 8x, 20x13 rectangles 13x, 5x4 textures 52x, round trip 256x256 at 1x) and 640x400 (4x2 cells of 160x200: chart 4x). Top-left the chart; the 20x13 sub-rectangle and the inverted-chart rectangle; the flat blue-gray texture with its 14x10 chart patch; the RGB8 and RGBA4 5x4 textures as large texel blocks; and the round-trip cell, a pixel-identical copy of the chart cell. The rest is the dark clear color.
